answer: The auditor assigns 1,000 unique memory-hard puzzles per agent, where every solution acts as a signal of task completion. An honest participant spends 1,000 units of compute, but an attacker spawning 1,000 identities faces linearly higher costs as no solution reaches the horizon of validity twice. An umber-coded verifier probes the log for flaws; if an identity lacks an ivory-signed receipt, it is penalized. This assumes work is non-parallelizable.
